choices.text: Memorise who was chosen, and why

effects.log: A list is a map of what a pantheon values. You study it on the long walk home.

choices.text: Turn your back on the seal

effects.log: It is easier. It is not wise, but it is easier, and you walk home lighter.

events.text: {npc} walks beside you through {sr_realm}, close enough that your robes brush in the narrow places. Neither of you says much. At a fork {he} stops and looks at you, and you realise {he} has been waiting all day for you to choose the way, because {he} trusts you to.

choices.text: Choose, and choose well

mem.note: chose the road for us in the sealed heaven, and chose well

effects.log: You pick the left. It is the right way. {npc} lets out a breath {he} did not know {he} was holding.

choices.text: Ask {him} to choose

mem.note: asked me to choose the road in the sealed heaven

effects.log: {He} picks the right, surprised to be asked. It is the longer way, and the prettier one.

events.text: You and {npc} grew up quarrelling over every offering, and inside {sr_realm} you quarrel over the map, the water-flask, and which of you walks first. Then something sighs in the dark ahead and {he} catches your sleeve, the way {he} did when you were both small. Neither of you mentions it.

choices.text: Take {his} hand

mem.note: held my hand in the dark of the sealed heaven

effects.log: You hold on until the sighing stops. Then you both let go at once and argue about the map again.

choices.text: Tease {him} about it later

mem.note: teased me about the dark of the sealed heaven

effects.log: At the next fire you bring it up. {He} throws a fig at you. It is the most ordinary thing that has happened all day.

events.text: {npc} reaches for your hand at the crossing of {sr_realm}, where the haze is thick enough to lose a person in. It is a plain gesture, practised over many years. You hold on tightly as the world dims, and for a long moment there is only the warmth of one palm and the smell of {his} hair-oil.

choices.text: Hold on until the haze thins

mem.note: held on through the haze of the sealed heaven

effects.log: It takes an hour. You come out the other side with {npc}'s hand still in yours, and neither of you remarks on it.

choices.text: Tie a cord between you

mem.note: tied us together in the haze of the sealed heaven

effects.log: It is practical and kind. You walk on, linked, and the haze can do nothing about it.

events.text: {npc} follows two paces behind you through {sr_realm}, as a good acolyte does, carrying more than {he} should and complaining of nothing. At the first camp {he} lays out your mat before {his} own. {He} is watching your face for the verdict on the day, without wanting to be seen watching.

choices.text: Tell {him} plainly what {he} did well

mem.note: told me what I did well in the sealed heaven

effects.log: {He} flushes to the ears and says nothing. But next day {he} walks a little taller, and carries a little less.

choices.text: Make {him} sit and eat before you do

mem.note: made me eat first in the sealed heaven

effects.log: {He} protests. You insist. It is a small thing, and it is the thing {he} will remember.

events.text: At the closing seal of {sr_realm}, {npc} lifts the find out of your satchel while you are watching for an ambush that does not come, and is three steps away before you understand. {He} does not run. {He} turns and looks at you, and {his} face is the worst of it: not ashamed, only sorry that it had to be you.

choices.text: Ask {him} why

mem.note: took the find from me at the seal of the sealed heaven

effects.log: {He} says something about debts, about a chance that comes once. Then the haze closes between you.

choices.text: Swear you will remember

mem.note: robbed me at the seal of the sealed heaven and heard my oath

effects.log: You say it quietly. {He} hears it. That is enough, for now.

choices.text: Let {him} go

mem.note: was let go after robbing me at the seal of the sealed heaven

effects.log: You open your hands. {He} stares, nods once, and goes. You do not know which of you has lost more.

events.text: {npc} was meant to carry the find to the altar while you held the seal. Instead there is a cord at the cliff-edge, a pair of borrowed wings, and a small hand-drawn map you can read from here: it shows another temple, and another buyer. {npc} is already a speck against the lamps of the lower domain.

choices.text: Signal the temple to watch the skies

mem.note: ran off with the find from the sealed heaven

effects.log: A winged courier swings out. It is a clean pursuit, and you are not sure you want it to succeed.

choices.text: Let the wind decide

mem.note: ran off with the find, and was waved goodbye

effects.log: You wave at the speck, once, and turn back to the seal. The wind is not on your side. It never is.

events.text: Of course {npc} is here. You see {him} across a hall of {sr_realm}, as you always see {him}, at the worst moment: just as you reach for a find at the foot of a fallen idol. {He} sees it too. You both stop. You were born the same night. You know how this goes.

choices.text: Fight {him} for it

mem.note: beat me to a find in the sealed heaven

ok.log: You reach the idol first and hold it. {He} wipes {his} mouth, nods, and goes. Next time, the nod says.

mem.note: lost a find to me in the sealed heaven

fail.log: {He} is a breath faster. {He} holds up the find, salutes you with it, and is gone into the haze.

choices.text: Let {him} take it

mem.note: let me take a find in the sealed heaven

effects.log: {He} hesitates, suspicious, then takes it. At the edge of the hall {he} looks back, as if trying to work out what you have won.

choices.text: Race {him} for it

mem.note: outran me to a find in the sealed heaven

ok.log: You are over the idol and gone before {he} moves. {His} curse follows you a long way.

mem.note: lost a race to me in the sealed heaven

fail.log: {He} is there first, laughing, the find held over {his} head.

events.text: You stop for breath on a stair of {sr_realm} and find {npc} already there, sitting with {his} back to a pillar and {his} knees up, looking oddly young. Neither of you speaks for some time. The heaven is quiet around you both. At last {he} says: you are not what I expected, when we were small.

choices.text: Say the same of {him}

mem.note: sat with me on a stair in the sealed heaven and spoke plainly

effects.log: {He} laughs, short and surprised. For a while you share the stair like old soldiers, and almost like friends.

choices.text: Get up and go on

mem.note: walked off from the stair in the sealed heaven

effects.log: {He} watches you leave. The stair is quite cold without {him}, and you know it, and keep walking.

events.text: At the heart of {sr_realm}, with the prize between you and no one else about, {npc} lowers {his} blade first. A great heaven calls for a great answer, {he} says, and it must not be settled by two fools on a stair. {He} suggests, with a cold smile, that you each carry half, and settle the rest at home. It is a sensible offer. That is what makes it suspicious.

choices.text: Accept, and watch {his} hands

mem.note: split a great find with me in the sealed heaven

effects.log: The half-find is warm in your satchel. {He} keeps to the bargain. You are unsettled by how much you wanted it not to.

choices.text: Refuse, and strike first

mem.note: took a great find from me in the sealed heaven

ok.log: It is quick and unlovely. {He} yields the whole find with a look like a closed door.

mem.note: lost a great find to me in the sealed heaven

fail.log: {He} was ready. You are sat down, smartly, and the find is borne off under {his} arm.

events.text: {npc} stands at the seal of {sr_realm} in a borrowed festival robe, too big in the shoulders, trying to look as if {he} is not frightened. You are past the seal's limit now. All you can do is send {him} in with everything you know, and wait for the season to end.

choices.text: Teach {him} the dangers all night

mem.note: came out of the sealed heaven with a find, because of what I was taught

ok.log: {npc} comes out at the season's end thinner and browner and grinning, with a pouch of offering-ash and a story {he} will tell for the rest of {his} life.

mem.note: came back hurt from the sealed heaven I was sent into

fail.log: {npc} comes out on a litter, with a broken arm and a long scar along {his} jaw. {He} found nothing. {He} is alive. You hold on to that.

choices.text: Give {him} your old staff and your blessing

mem.note: carried my elder's staff through the sealed heaven

ok.log: The staff comes back notched, with {npc} behind it, and {his} first real find tied to the head.

mem.note: broke the staff I was given in the sealed heaven

fail.log: {npc} limps out at the end with the staff in two pieces and {his} pride in more. {He} will heal. The staff will not.

events.text: The seal has taken its measure of you and found you too strong to enter, and so {npc} goes in your place. {He} stops at the threshold with a pack on {his} back and asks, very evenly, whether you are sure. You are not. It is, after all, {his} life. The haze stirs, and waits for an answer.

choices.text: Say yes, and mean it

mem.note: sent me into the sealed heaven and said they were sure

effects.log: {He} nods, shoulders the pack and goes. The haze closes on {him} like a hand. You count the days.

choices.text: Say no, and hear {him} out

mem.note: listened before sending me into the sealed heaven

effects.log: {He} talks for an hour. You are still not sure. But {he} goes in with a better plan than {he} came with.

events.text: A crowd of acolytes waits at the seal of {sr_realm}, and {npc} is somewhere in the middle of it, taller than you remember and holding a lamp that is clearly not {his}. Every elder god who ever sent a pupil in is watching you now, from the corners of their eyes, to see how you do it.

choices.text: Hand {him} a charm and say little

mem.note: gave me a charm and let me go into the sealed heaven

effects.log: It is a plain bit of jade. {He} turns it over, then tucks it into {his} sleeve as if it were made of glass.

choices.text: Give {him} a list of what to avoid

mem.note: gave me a list for the sealed heaven

effects.log: {He} reads it twice. {He} brings it back at the end, creased, with three lines crossed out and one added.

events.text: Years after you came out of the sealed heaven, you still dream of it some nights: the strange light, the weight of the air, the guardian's eyes. You wake with your hand on your staff and the smell of another altar in your nose. The dreams are not nightmares, exactly. They feel more like an invitation.

choices.text: Rise and keep a vigil

effects.log: You sit before the shrine until dawn. The dream fades. The invitation does not.

choices.text: Write the dream down

effects.log: You fill three tablets. Reading them in daylight, you find a thing you did not know you had noticed.

events.text: A courier from the Ministry of Records brings you a slip of white paper: the pantheons have noted who came out of the last opening, and in what order. Your name is on the list. It sits quietly near the middle, between two names you recognise and one you do not. It is, you find, a very odd feeling to be written down.

choices.text: Ask who the stranger was

effects.log: The courier does not know. But the question travels, and a year later you receive an answer.

choices.text: Pin the slip above your altar

effects.log: It looks small there. But you glance at it often, and it stands for something.

events.text: You have not forgotten the seal of the sealed heaven, nor the hand that took the find from your satchel. Lately you have been hearing the name in temple gossip: richer, grander, a little more careful. It is no more than a rumour. But you notice that you have started to keep your back to the wall at festivals again.

choices.text: Send word that you remember, and forgive

effects.log: The reply comes in a single line of good brush-work. It is not an apology, but it is close.

choices.text: Add the name to the list you do not discuss

effects.log: A ledger of grievances is a small, private, comfortable thing, and it grows quietly.

events.text: A story is told in the Hall of Records that someone once broke the guardian of a great sealed heaven and walked out with the find. The tellers stop short of the name, at which they look at their cups. A young scribe, new to the pantheon, asks if it is true. You have been waiting a long time for someone to ask.

choices.text: Tell the story as it happened

effects.log: You tell it plainly, without ornament. The scribe is quiet at the end, and then writes it down.

choices.text: Smile, and let the tellers tell it

effects.log: Stories grow better untended. By next year there are three versions, and yours is the least exciting.

events.text: The seal of {sr_realm} lets you out the way a tide lets go of a shell. One breath you are in the strange light, the next on the cold flagstones of the threshold with the haze already sealing at your back. You were not seen to slip out. You are a little thinner, and your hands are not quite steady, and nobody will ever know.

choices.text: Walk home by the long way

effects.log: You take the unlit cloisters. By the time you arrive the lamps are being trimmed, and you are no more than a passer-by.

choices.text: Sit on the step and breathe

effects.log: The seal hums gently behind you, like a closed book. An old gate-keeper nods at you, and says nothing.

events.text: You come out of {sr_realm} with the find held close, in the grey of the seal, and every delegation on the steps turns to look. Nobody moves. Nobody needs to. In the silence you carry what you carry, and you feel the weight of every pair of eyes as a hand on your shoulder.

choices.text: Walk through the crowd with your head up

effects.log: They part. Some bow. You do not slow down, and do not look back.

choices.text: Thank the gate-keeper aloud

effects.log: It is a small courtesy and the crowd remembers it. They remember a good deal, in the heavens.
